title: Requests and load
description: API requests by route, status and user ID, and what they cost: the database pool, live connections, memory and CPU (R72), and how far a re-parse has got (R23b). Grafana's own trace links open Explore at its default "Last 1 hour"; this dashboard's links ("Open in Explore (this time range)", "Open the trace (this time range)") carry the dashboard's time range.

options.content:
**Prometheus** counts every request the API answers, by route and status (never the real path). **Tempo** keeps each request's trace, with the signed-in user's numeric ID and role, nothing else about them (R70). Each panel's **i** says what normal looks like. In short, worry when **errors** appear, when the **slowest 10 %** stays up, when the **database pool** runs out (in use at max, waits climbing), or when **memory** or **goroutines** keep rising without falling back. At the bottom, **Re-parse** says Idle, or, after an alias, template or profile change, how far re-parsing the stored messages has got, how fast it goes and about how long it has left, or that an admin paused or stopped it. Below it, **Retroactive redaction** does the same for the nightly run's check of every stored message after the redaction rules change.

The graphs from traces: click a line to pin its tooltip, then **Open in Explore (this time range)** lists that user's requests or that query's runs, in this dashboard's time range. A dot is a sample request: click it for its trace. A trace opens whatever time range Explore shows.

panels.title: Requests per second, by route and status
panels.description: How many requests the API answers each second, by route and status. Normal: browsers' lists and live updates, receiving clients' posts, and Alloy's scrape of /metrics every 15 s, mostly status 200. Worry: a 401 or 403 line that keeps going (a client with a wrong key, or someone failing to sign in), any 5xx (see Errors), or a steady climb when nobody's using the archive (something polling).

panels.title: Slowest 10 % of requests, by route (dots are sample requests: click one for its trace)
panels.description: How long the slowest 10 % of requests to each route took: 9 in 10 were faster. Normal: tens of milliseconds; searches, reports and exports take longer. Worry: a route that stays slow for minutes. Click a dot, a sample request, then "Open the trace (this time range)" to see which step took the time.

panels.title: Requests per second, by user ID (from traces)
panels.description: Requests each second from each signed-in user, by their numeric ID (PagerArchive's /admin/users/ID page says who it is). Normal: a few a second while someone browses, then nothing. Worry: one ID making requests steadily for hours: a script, or a tab left polling. Click a line, then "Open in Explore (this time range)" for that user's requests.

panels.title: Recent requests by signed-in users (user ID and role only, R70)
panels.description: The newest requests from signed-in users in the time range: user ID, role, route and status. Click a span ID to open that request's trace.

targets.query: {span.user.id != nil && kind=server} | select(span.user.id, span.user.role, span.http.route, span.http.response.status_code)

panels.title: Errors (5xx) per second, by route
panels.description: Requests the API failed (status 5xx) each second, by route. Normal: empty. Worry: any line at all. The API's log and the failed request's trace say why: the trace's error span names the kind of error.

panels.title: Abandoned requests per minute, by route
panels.description: Requests the browser or client gave up on before the API answered (R73a): the tab closed, the phone lost its signal, or the person moved on. They're answered 499, logged at INFO and aren't errors. Normal: a few now and then, mostly on the slower routes. Worry: a route climbing steadily: its pages are slow enough that people give up waiting. "Slowest 10 % of requests" above shows how slow.

panels.title: Database: slowest 10 % by query (from traces)
panels.description: How long the slowest 10 % of runs of each database query took, by the query's name. Normal: a few milliseconds; searches and reports take longer. Worry: one query climbing week by week as the archive grows, or a query suddenly slow for everyone. Click a line, then "Open in Explore (this time range)" for that query's runs and their traces.

panels.title: Database pool
panels.description: The API keeps a few database connections open and lends one to each request that needs the database. in_use: lent out now; idle: open and free; max: the most it will open; waits per second: requests that found none free and had to wait. Normal: in_use mostly 0 or 1, waits near 0. Worry: in_use at max and waits climbing: requests are queueing for a connection, so everything slows. Look for a slow query in the panel above, or more load than the pool is sized for.

panels.title: Open live-update connections (browsers and watches)
panels.description: Connections held open for live updates: one per browser tab showing a list, and one per PowerShell watch (R63b). Normal: about the number of tabs and watches open. Worry: many more than the people using it, or a count that only ever climbs: connections aren't being closed.

panels.title: API memory (budget 256 MiB)
panels.description: resident: the memory the API's process holds, which the 256 MiB budget (section 8) counts; the red line is the budget. Go heap in use: the part taken by the API's own data. Normal: well under the line, rising during an import, a report or the nightly jobs and falling back after. Worry: a steady rise towards the line that never falls back: a leak.

panels.title: API CPU (share of one core)
panels.description: How much of one CPU core the API uses: 100 % is a whole core. Normal: near 0 at rest, with short spikes for searches, imports and the nightly jobs. Worry: staying high when nobody's using the archive.

panels.title: Goroutines
panels.description: Goroutines are the API's lightweight threads: each request in progress, live-update connection and background job runs in one or more. Normal: a steady few dozen, going up and down with requests and live connections. Worry: a count that keeps climbing for hours without falling back: something is stuck or leaking, and memory usually climbs with it.

panels.title: Re-parse
panels.description: The re-parse's state (R23a-R23c): after an alias, template or profile changes, the API re-parses and re-places the affected messages in the background. A profile change re-parses the whole archive, which takes hours on a large one. Running; Paused or Stopped when an admin paused or stopped it (Administration, Re-parse, or the PowerShell module). A restart or upgrade carries a running one on from where it got to. Normal: Idle, or Running for a while after a change. Worry: Running with no change made, or Paused or Stopped and forgotten: changes made meanwhile wait for it.

panels.title: Re-parse progress
panels.description: How much of this re-parse is done: messages re-parsed so far against the number it had to do, counted when it started. Pages that arrive meanwhile are re-parsed too, so it can sit at 100 % for a moment. At 100 % it's rebuilding the large events around the pages it touched (R87f), until "Re-parse" says Idle. Paused or stopped, it stays where it got to. Normal: climbing steadily. Worry: stuck at the same number for many minutes: the API's log has "re-parse progress" every 30 s (done, total, percent, per_minute, eta_seconds).

panels.title: Re-parsed per minute
panels.description: How fast this re-parse is going: messages re-parsed a minute, over the last 5 minutes. It depends on the archive (pages with addresses take longer) and the host. Normal: steady while it runs. Worry: falling towards 0 while Re-parse says Running: something is holding it up (the database, or the host's CPU).

panels.title: Re-parse time left
panels.description: About how long this re-parse has left: the messages still to do at the last 5 minutes' rate. Normal: going down. Worry: going up: it's slowing down (see Re-parsed per minute).

panels.title: Re-parse: messages to do and done
panels.description: Each re-parse's messages to do (counted when it started) and done so far, over the dashboard's time range. While none runs, both stay at the last run's numbers, done equal to to do. Normal: done climbing in a straight line up to to do. Worry: done flat while Re-parse says Running, or a run that starts again from 0 without finishing that no one started again (an admin's Start again, or a changed profile at start-up, do). A restart carries a run on from where it got to, so done doesn't drop then; while Paused or Stopped, done stays flat.

panels.title: Retroactive redaction
panels.description: Retroactive redaction's state (P1, R45a): when the network profile's redaction rules change, the nightly run checks every stored message against them, and writes each changed message's new text and its re-parse together. On a large archive that takes hours. Running; Paused or Stopped when an admin paused or stopped it (Administration, Retroactive redaction, or the PowerShell module). A restart or upgrade carries a running one on from where it got to, at once; the next nightly run starts a stopped one again. Normal: Idle, or Running for a while after the rules changed. Worry: Paused and forgotten: the messages it hasn't reached still hold what the new rules remove.

panels.title: Retroactive redaction progress
panels.description: How much of this run is done: messages checked so far against the number stored when it started. Messages that arrive meanwhile are checked too, so it can sit at 100 % for a moment; then it drops the imported source IDs the rules match and rebuilds the large events around the messages it changed, until Retroactive redaction says Idle. Paused or stopped, it stays where it got to. Normal: climbing steadily. Worry: stuck at the same number for many minutes: the API's log has "retroactive redaction progress" every 30 s (done, total, percent, per_minute, eta_seconds).

panels.title: Redaction checked per minute
panels.description: How fast this run is going: messages checked a minute, over the last 5 minutes. Messages the rules don't change are quick; each one they change is re-parsed too, at about the re-parse's rate. Normal: steady while it runs. Worry: falling towards 0 while Retroactive redaction says Running: something is holding it up (the database, or the host's CPU).

panels.title: Redaction time left
panels.description: About how long this run has left: the messages still to check at the last 5 minutes' rate. Normal: going down. Worry: going up: it's slowing down (see Redaction checked per minute).

panels.title: Retroactive redaction: messages to check and checked
panels.description: Each run's messages to check (counted when it started) and checked so far, over the dashboard's time range. While none runs, both stay at the last run's numbers. Normal: checked climbing in a straight line up to to check. Worry: checked flat while Retroactive redaction says Running. A restart carries a run on from where it got to, so checked doesn't drop then; an admin's Start again, changed rules at start-up, or the nightly run starting a stopped run again, start from 0; while Paused or Stopped, it stays flat.
